key_fields.sql: select z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone, count(t.pulocationid) as cash_trips from ops.zones z left join lake.trips t on t.pulocationid = z.locationid and t.payment_type = 2 group by z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone order by z.locationid
key_fields.claim: The sequential scan on trips reads all rows to evaluate payment_type=2; creating an index on payment_type (if DuckDB supported secondary indexes) or partitioning the table by payment_type would avoid the full scan.

value.sql: SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips FROM ops.zones z LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2 GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone ORDER BY z.LocationID
value.change_summary: No rewrite possible without indexes; query already uses optimal hash join and grouping order for DuckDB columnar engine.
value.risk_notes: Performance depends on DuckDB's internal optimizations; cannot force index usage as DuckDB lacks secondary indexes on Parquet tables.
